thread:
jia: quick summary of the kernel sweep I ran across regions/GPUs — TL;DR: FlashAttention v3 wins for long seqs on H100, Triton custom kernels are competitive at short seqs and lower memory configs, vendor libs (NVIDIA heuristics) still matter for mixed-precision and int8 paths.

marco: nice — which models and seq lengths?

jia: ran a 7B LLM (decoder-only transformer) and a 30B candidate. Seq lens: 128, 512, 2048. Batch sizes 1/4/8 depending on memory. Regions: us-west (h100), us-east (a100), eu-central (nv4-like ampere instances).

emma: numbers? charts? :eyes:

jia: pasted the minimal ascii summary below (median latency in ms, p95, tokens/sec for b=4 where applicable). these are end-to-end inference numbers (prompt+generation of 128 tokens) on 32k context disabled.

--- 7B model (seq=512, gen=128, b=1) ---
H100 (us-west):
  FlashAttn v3  median=58ms  p95=95ms  toks/s=1800
  Triton kernel   median=72ms  p95=120ms toks/s=1400
  Vendor lib (heuristic) median=65ms p95=110ms toks/s=1600

A100 (us-east):
  FlashAttn v3  median=68ms  p95=110ms toks/s=1500
  Triton kernel   median=70ms  p95=115ms toks/s=1440
  Vendor lib      median=66ms  p95=108ms toks/s=1520

nv4 (eu-central):
  FlashAttn v3  median=92ms  p95=140ms toks/s=1100
  Triton kernel   median=88ms  p95=135ms toks/s=1150
  Vendor lib      median=95ms  p95=150ms toks/s=1050

--- 7B model (seq=2048, b=1) ---
H100 (us-west):
  FlashAttn v3  median=240ms p95=370ms toks/s=680
  Triton kernel   median=330ms p95=480ms toks/s=520
  Vendor lib      median=290ms p95=420ms toks/s=600

notes: v3 shows large relative gains as seq grows (memory access optimizations + tiled attention). Triton does better for short seq/low memory because our custom launcher overlaps IO better in those cases.

ryan: what about quantized runs? any quality regressions?

jia: ran q4_0 and int8-ish paths. For q4_0 on 7B: latency improved 15-25% (model-dependent). Quality (measured on our eval bank of 200 prompts, aggregated F1-style score) dropped by ~0.6% absolute for q4_0 vs fp16 for 7B. int8 path (experimental vendor lib) gave 30-40% speedup but quality drop ~1.8% on same eval set — borderline for prod.

anita: did you check failure modes (hallucination, tokenization edge cases) after quant?

jia: yes — regression alerts pick up a handful of hallucination-style failures in q4_0 for long-context retrieval prompts at seq>1024. We should gate q4_0 behind targeted evals for customers who care about long-context RAG.

emma: kernel switching heuristic idea?

jia: propose an automatic policy in runtime:
  - if seq <= 256 and batch <= 4: prefer Triton kernel (lower tail latency)
  - if seq in (257..1024): prefer vendor lib unless H100 with FlashAttn v3 available -> prefer FA v3 on H100
  - if seq > 1024: prefer FlashAttention v3 on H100/A100; fallback to vendor lib otherwise
  - if quant_mode == q4_0: require eval pass; if quality drop > 1% then disable for route

marco: sounds good. how about memory / capacity sizing? numbers to convert to units?

jia: rough capacity guidance (7B model, steady gen of 32 tokens per request, 30 rps total across a pool):
  - H100 with FAv3: 1 instance ~ 120 rps (small-request mix), so for 30 rps you need 1 instance with room.
  - A100 (vendor heuristics): 1 instance ~ 90 rps.
  - nv4: 1 instance ~ 45 rps.
So for global pool with 50% us-west, 30% us-east, 20% eu: provision 1 h100, 1 a100, 1 nv4 for buffer and failover; autoscale rules for bursts.

ryan: did you test mixed-precision kernel composition? e.g., fa v3 attention + triton matmuls?

jia: yes — hybrid composition works but scheduling becomes tricky. We saw ~3-5% added overhead due to extra kernel launches and cross-kernel sync. Not worth mixing unless you have memory/compat constraints. Prefer single optimized path per request.

emma: any regressions pinned to v3 vs v2?

jia: v3 fixed a few perf cliffs for heads>8 and variable-seqlen batch packing. We saw no accuracy regressions between v2 and v3 on our evals. Biggest difference is memory layout requirements — v3 needs workspace alignment which our allocator handled but some custom quant paths needed small adapters.

jia: 1) add FA v3 to model profiles for H100-backed routes, 2) add runtime policy rules from above, 3) run extended eval (1k prompts) on q4_0 for long-context customers and block auto-quant if regressions exceed threshold. I'll open PR with the rack plan + perf artifacts.

jia: will do — thanks.
